name: API Uptime
blurb:
This section tracks measured uptime for 12 AI API providers, including Anthropic, OpenAI, Cohere, Groq, Cerebras, Deepgram, ElevenLabs, AssemblyAI, Stability AI, Baseten, Fireworks AI, and Lambda. For each provider it records a healthy or unhealthy status at each check and rolls that up into a healthy percentage over the tracked window, alongside a daily count of how many providers are currently healthy.

The status comes from automated checks against each provider's own reported status, run several times a day since mid-August 2026, not from independent synthetic testing of the live API endpoints. That means it reflects what providers disclose about their own availability, which can lag or understate real user-facing disruptions, and short blips between checks may not register at all. It is a directional reliability signal across providers, not a service-level guarantee.

As of September 5, 2026, all 12 tracked providers show healthy status, matching the pattern for most of the past week. Over the full tracked period, reliability is uneven. Lambda stands out as the clear laggard at 56.3 percent healthy across 142 checks, far below the rest of the field. OpenAI is next weakest at 88.5 percent, with Fireworks AI and Anthropic both around 95.9 percent. Six providers, including Groq, Deepgram, AssemblyAI, and Stability AI, recorded 100 percent healthy checks across the entire window.

reading.body:
Six of twelve tracked AI API providers report perfect uptime across the measured window from mid-August to early September 2026, but two major providers lag significantly behind, with operational consistency varying enough to matter for production deployments.

Lambda is a clear outlier, reporting healthy status only 61.7 percent of the time across 162 checks. OpenAI follows at 89.9 percent healthy, meaning users experienced unavailability roughly one day per ten. The remaining ten providers cluster above 96 percent, with AssemblyAI, Deepgram, Groq, and Stability AI all recording 100 percent uptime across the full window.

This data reflects only what providers disclose about themselves, not independent testing of actual user-facing availability. Providers may underreport disruptions, and brief outages between checks can vanish from the record. The measurement also cannot distinguish between brief blips and extended service loss. Recent stability is notably better than the full period, with all twelve providers reporting healthy status most days since late August, suggesting either improving conditions or a statistical tail-off toward the present.

For applications requiring continuous inference throughput, relying on a single provider introduces material risk. The gap between Lambda and the field, or between OpenAI and smaller competitors, suggests infrastructure maturity and operational investment vary substantially across the ecosystem, which may reflect different scaling speeds or compute constraints at the backend.
